- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.5), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for volatility.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction: if price spiked 3%+ in last 3 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3 periods.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a “mean reversion” rule: forecast = 0.8×previous + 0.2×true recent 3-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict in early periods when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day average to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral), model often underperforms; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for low sentiment bias.
